title: Timed spot urinary creatinine adds a small, training-sensitive grip-strength prediction gain across NHANES samples
abstract: A source-frozen model trained in3846 NHANES2011–2012 adults was tested in4266 separately sampled2013–2014 adults. Adding log timed spot urinary creatinine excretion beyond anthropometry, age, sex and serum/urine creatinine reduced weighted combined-grip RMSE11.791171 to11.727697kg. Conditional target PSU bootstrap95% delta interval[-0.121032,-0.008140]kg excluded zero; source/target coefficient-refit interval[-0.116395,+0.015180] did not. A flexible comparator retained a small gain. The signal is tentative, equivalent to additional log-flow information in unpenalized regression, and not uniquely attributable to muscle. Same-program independent-sample testing is not independent-study validation. Reproducible offline analysis, author checks and clean rerun are provided; no clinical utility or causal claim.
